plotting_plan.title: Provenance-first pipeline with database-held-out evaluation
plotting_plan.objective: Left-to-right block diagram in two horizontal lanes separated by a labelled wall. TOP LANE, 'extraction (pipeline/extract; frozen 2026-10-20, pre-registration v1.0)': (1) Corpus: PubMed search + backward citation search, title/abstract screening by Sonnet helpers, full-text screening; open access only (PMC, Europe PMC, Unpaywall; D-32) (log §1.4). (2) Extraction: one Claude Opus helper per paper reads only that paper + frozen files (extract_v6, schema v5, rules v1) and writes five tables (publications, individuals, variants, phenotypic_features, 20-item phenotype checklist); every value = value + verbatim quote + PMID; phenotypes three-state observed / excluded / not reported (idea.md Core idea 1-2; log §1.5, §1.7). (3) Deterministic span check: every quote found verbatim in the paper. (4) Gatekeeper v4: a second Claude read of every claim; verdicts supported / partially supported / unsupported / span not found; only supported claims go on (idea.md 3; log §1.7). (5) Stage 4: reconciliation (citation-only, one-to-one merges, policy v4), VariantValidator normalization on MANE Select keeping the original string, HPO / Mondo binding (pinned releases) (log §1.7). (6) Output: GA4GH Phenopackets v2, schema-validated. WALL between lanes labelled 'isolation test: no ClinVar / OMIM in extraction' (log §1.8). BOTTOM LANE, 'harness (held-out ground truth, read only after extraction)': dated ClinVar snapshot and OMIM entry pages frozen 2026-10-28 -> O2 concordance and O3 gap candidates (absent from ClinVar and OMIM) -> evidence dossiers (verbatim quotes, no proposed classification) -> people: O1 audit of gatekeeper-supported claims, triage of ClinVar misses, gap adjudication (pointer 'see Figure fig_human_assessment'). Arrows from Output (6) and from the gatekeeper-supported claim pool (4) down into the harness lane. Small badges, text only, no outcome values: '241,730 values, 0 span-check problems (registered six)' at the span check (log §2.1.2) is the only number allowed. Do not draw ClinVar or OMIM feeding into any top-lane box.

plotting_plan.title: Human assessment: calibration, then rotating groups of raters
plotting_plan.objective: Design diagram of the D-55 human assessment (log §4), left to right, with no results and no rater names. STAGE 1 'Calibration (due 2026-11-22)': box 'reference labels by the PI on 99 candidate claims from the registered runs, blind to the gatekeeper' -> box 'fixed set rule (+2 recorded amendments) -> 40 claims: 20 unsupported, 20 supported, 39 papers' -> nine identical small rater icons labelled R1...R9 (same 40 claims, each in its own order; no reference label, gatekeeper verdict or source pool shown) -> diamond 'floor: >=15 of 20 unsupported caught AND >=18 of 20 supported passed' (log §4.1). Do not show which kind of claim was capped or the cap size. DECISION node 'PI decides after calibration: who goes on; Plan A (registered six) or Plan B (all twelve)' with two branches annotated by planning figures from log §4.3: Plan A = 250 audit claims, 50 ClinVar misses, 214 gap candidates; Plan B = 527, 146, 269. STAGE 2 'Main assessment' as three parallel tracks: (a) Audit: each claim read by 3 raters in rotating overlapping groups of three (84 groups with nine raters), equal loads, every pair shares claims; script names a registered pair + tie-breaker per claim; rule C: at most 4 of 250 unsupported. (b) Triage of ClinVar misses: 2 raters per item, PI settles differences. (c) Gap adjudication: 2 raters per candidate, a third where they differ on the decision or across the pathogenic / uncertain line. All three tracks end at a box 'panel approval + PI sign-off before any submission record' (nothing submitted yet). Draw rotating groups as a small ring of 9 nodes with three overlapping triangles to suggest overlap. No numbers other than those listed here.

introduction_strategy.hook_hypothesis: Rare-disease genotype-phenotype knowledge is fragmented: variants sit in ClinVar and OMIM, phenotype vocabulary in HPO, a small share of cases in phenopacket-store, and most individual patients only in published case reports, so a laboratory querying ClinVar cannot see a causative variant that was published but never submitted (idea.md Problem). Use the corrected Alexander disease figures as the concrete hook: about 550 published patients and 182 causative variants (2024 meta-analysis) against 76 ClinVar P/LP records (release 2026-10-12) and 13 OMIM allelic variants (gene entry frozen 2026-10-28) (log §1.11; never the application's 72 / ~12). None of the twelve genes has a folder in phenopacket-store (735 gene folders at commit ca133e6, 2026-11-04; log §1.2). Diseases recur faster than hand curation, so the need is a pipeline that can be pointed at any disease with provenance a clinician can check.
introduction_strategy.problem_gap_hypothesis: Prior LLM and text-mining work extracts variants or HPO terms, but rarely (i) attaches a verbatim, machine-checked quote to every value with 'not reported' as a first-class output, (ii) evaluates against reference databases kept strictly out of extraction, and (iii) separates a model's self-check from a human-measured error rate. Scope the gap strictly to what this report evaluates: a frozen, pre-registered pipeline run on six registered rare diseases (plus five extension diseases and one exploratory disease reported apart), with automatic concordance against ClinVar/OMIM and gap candidates; its human-measured accuracy (O1, the primary outcome) is pending, written as \HR{o1_unsupported_n} of 250. The introduction must say early, in a short status paragraph, that every human result is a boxed placeholder to be filled by script, that the two pre-freeze pilot audits were above the 2% target (6.0%, 3/50; 6.3%, 3/48), and that this is version 4 of an internal interim report superseding versions 2 (2026-10-28) and 3 (2026-11-02). End with contributions exactly as idea.md 'Contributions' states them (pipeline under a frozen pre-registration on twelve diseases; database-held-out evaluation with dossiers ready for adjudication; an honest account of what is not yet known). Do not claim accuracy, submissions, or that pilot results generalize; do not mention the SLIDERS ablation.
search_directions: Real-world impact of the literature-database gap in rare disease: evidence that disease-causing variants and patient-level phenotypes published in case reports are missing from ClinVar or other databases, and the cost of diagnostic delay (published before 2026-11).
Surveys and systematic reviews of large language models for biomedical information extraction, evidence synthesis and rare-disease genomics (published before 2026-11).

Foundational works on computable case-level rare-disease records: deep phenotyping with HPO, GA4GH Phenopackets, variant nomenclature, and variant classification standards (the canonical papers, any year).

related_work_strategy.overview: Three clusters, each ending with how GP-RareLink differs, scoped to what the log measures. Credit SLIDERS and the Lam lab's prior grounding/verification work (STORM, WikiChat) without implying the public SLIDERS code was run (log §1.1: a home-built version of the method, D-20). Keep the unfavourable related result: Claude Sonnet 4 had the lowest exact-count concordance (73.0%) of five models at counting probands (log §1.11). Use only the corrected wording for the application's benchmark claims (HPO 97.6% is from four synthetic notes, tool-augmented; 'DRBench' figures are hallucinated-URL rates).

subsections.subsection_title: 2.1 Variant and phenotype extraction from the biomedical literature
subsections.methodology_cluster: Text-mining and LLM systems that recognize and normalize variants (tmVar, LitVar, AVADA, PubMind, AutoPM3) and HPO concepts (PhenoTagger, PhenoGPT, RAG-HPO, SPIRES/OntoGPT, RARE-PHENIX, HPO-MCP), and LLM evidence extraction for clinical genomics (PS4 proband counting, functional evidence, disease-gene extraction, AI-CURA).
subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Find how these systems are evaluated (corpus type: case reports vs clinical notes vs abstracts; per-value provenance; negation/absence handling; comparison to curated databases) and what accuracies they report, up to 2026-11. Do not look for new competitors to benchmark; the only model comparison in the log is Claude vs DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash under an identical scaffold.
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: Most systems output entities or variant-paper links without a verbatim quote per value, collapse 'not reported' into absence, work on abstracts or clinical notes rather than full-text case reports, and score against annotations rather than held-out databases; LLM numeric/count fields are error-prone.
limitation_search_queries: large language model extraction of HGVS variants and HPO phenotypes from full-text case reports evaluated against ClinVar
patient-level phenotype extraction from rare disease case reports with negated or absent findings
subsections.bridge_to_our_method: GP-RareLink emits per-person three-state records with a machine-checked verbatim quote on every value (241,730 values, 0 span-check problems in the registered six; log §2.1.2) and keeps ClinVar/OMIM out of extraction so they can score it.

subsections.subsection_title: 2.2 LLM-assisted systematic review and verification of claims against cited evidence
subsections.methodology_cluster: LLM data extraction for evidence synthesis (SLIDERS, otto-SR, Gartlehner 2024, Kataoka 2025) and attribution/claim-verification methods (AIS, ALCE, FActScore, self-verification, chain-of-verification, VeriFact, SourceCheckup), with known limits of LLM self-correction and LLM-as-judge.
subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Collect how extraction accuracy is audited by humans (sample sizes, unit of audit, interval methods) and how LLM verifiers are validated against human labels, up to 2026-11.
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: LLM verifiers and self-checks are rarely calibrated against human labels and can favour outputs of the same model family; reported extraction accuracies come from small samples without pre-registered decision rules.
limitation_search_queries: human audit of large language model data extraction for systematic reviews unsupported or incorrect values
validation of LLM fact-checker or attribution judge against human labels sensitivity
subsections.bridge_to_our_method: The gatekeeper checks each value strictly against its own quote, but its rate is reported as a model reading, not an error rate (pilot: humans ~6% unsupported where the gatekeeper found 0.04-0.3%); the primary outcome is a pre-registered 250-claim human audit with rule C, preceded by rater calibration on reference labels (log §1.9, §2.1.5, §4).

subsections.subsection_title: 2.3 Case-level rare-disease resources, imperfect reference databases, and memorization
subsections.methodology_cluster: Hand-curated phenopacket corpora (phenopacket-store, pyphetools/phenopacket-tools, GPSEA), LLM diagnosis benchmarks built on phenopackets, ClinVar classification discordance and misclassification, incomplete disease-phenotype annotations, ascertainment bias in literature cohorts, and data-contamination/memorization probes.
subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Find evidence on how far ClinVar/OMIM can serve as ground truth for literature-derived records, how literature-derived phenotype frequencies deviate from genotype-first or natural-history cohorts, and black-box memorization probes usable on closed models, up to 2026-11.
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: Curated case-level corpora do not scale to diseases nobody has curated; databases used as ground truth are themselves incomplete or wrong; benchmarks built from published cases risk training-data leakage.
limitation_search_queries: ClinVar as reference standard limitations for literature-derived variant curation concordance
black-box memorization or data contamination probe for large language models on biomedical publications
subsections.bridge_to_our_method: GP-RareLink treats database misses as items for human triage rather than automatic errors, reports OMIM as a human-curated holdout (57.3%, 43/75), and ran a memorization probe on 180 papers in which neither model reproduced the papers' variants or text (log §2.1.6, §2.1.7, §2.1.9).

subsections.subsection_title: Abstract (one paragraph)
content_bullets: One paragraph, ~200-230 words, no citations. Problem (idea.md Problem) and question (log §1.1).

Method in one sentence each: full-text extraction by Claude Opus helpers with a verbatim quote and PMID on every value and three-state phenotypes; a second Claude read (gatekeeper) on every claim; HGVS on MANE Select, HPO/Mondo binding, GA4GH Phenopackets v2; ClinVar and OMIM held out of extraction and used only to score; pre-registration and pipeline frozen 2026-10-20.

Registered six (primary): 350 papers, 2,836 phenopackets, all schema-valid; 241,730 values, every quote found verbatim (log §2.1.2, §2.1.4). Gatekeeper judged 0.43% (248/57,819) of claims unsupported in the five confirmatory diseases, stated as a model reading, not an error rate.

ClinVar HGVS recall low and concentrated in single papers (tier 1 10.1%-35.0%); OMIM allelic variants recovered 57.3% (43/75), bounded by literature access; 214 live gap candidates in the registered six (269 across all twelve) with evidence dossiers, none adjudicated or submitted (log §2.1.6-2.1.8, §2.0).
Beside the registered study (not pooled): five extension diseases, an exploratory twelfth disease and a corpus addendum; 665 paper-runs over twelve diseases (log §2.0).

Status sentence with placeholders: 'The primary outcome, a 250-claim human audit, found \HR{o1_unsupported_n} unsupported (\HR{o1_unsupported_pct}; exact 95% CI \HR{o1_unsupported_ci}); rule C: \HR{o1_rule_c}.' Mention that two pre-freeze pilot audits were above the 2% target (6.0%, 6.3%) and that nine volunteer raters are in a calibration round (due 2026-11-22). Never write 'only' or any direction next to a placeholder.

subsections.subsection_title: 3.2 Extraction with provenance and three-state phenotypes
content_bullets: The SLIDERS method (evidence tables with verbatim excerpts as provenance, code-writing reconciliation) run as a home-built version with Claude Code helper agents on the funded claude.ai account, not the public SLIDERS code (D-20, log §1.1, §1.6); credit SLIDERS and the Lam lab.

One Claude Opus helper per paper reads only its paper, the instruction file, the schema and the rules file; no web access; told not to use anything it remembers about the paper. Served model claude-opus-5-5 (registered manifests recorded the alias 'opus'; served_model added 2026-10-28, marked). No sampling parameters on this route; training cutoff June 2026 (log §1.6).

Four pinned files frozen 2026-10-20 (extract_v6, gatekeeper_v4, schema_ha20_v5 with five tables, extraction_rules_v1); per-disease instantiation swaps 12 lines and a 20-item checklist written from open guidelines/reviews with every quote checked (D-38; log §1.5).

Record rules: every value carries PMID + verbatim quote; deterministic span check on all values; 'not reported' is first-class and has no quote; normal findings recorded as excluded abnormality (D-27); variant fields only from statements about this person (D-29); no positional reading of stacked cells (D-31) (log §1.7).
